stemMd: A solution contains Ag⁺ ions. Which added ion is most likely to produce a poorly soluble precipitate under ordinary laboratory conditions?
explanationMd: Silver chloride is poorly soluble, so Ag⁺ + Cl⁻ → AgCl(s) can remove the ions from solution as a solid. Nitrate salts are generally soluble, while the listed cations do not provide the anion needed for this precipitation.

distractorRationale.a: Silver nitrate is soluble under ordinary conditions.
distractorRationale.e: A second cation does not pair with Ag⁺ to form the expected precipitate.
distractorRationale.d: Another alkali-metal cation does not provide the precipitating anion.
distractorRationale.c: Adding a cation alone does not form silver chloride.
